title: Non-string or variant SOS type values fall through and activate
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:213-216: the cancel branch matches body['type'] == 'cancel' exactly. A bytes-typed CBOR type (b'cancel' != 'cancel', verified) or variant token ('Cancel') falls through the pass into the ACTIVATION path, so a properly-signed cancel with a mis-encoded type returns CREATED and activates. Security-neutral today (signature must verify over that exact core, so only the originator's own mis-encoding is affected; C parity: sos_alert.c:403-410 uses exact strcmp). Fix: strict-type the branch (isinstance str) and/or whitelist activation types {sos, medical, security, fire} and reject unknown types with 4.00 instead of silently reinterpreting.
